_about: The manifest of a research area (a 'pack'). This is the TEMPLATE: a complete, working pack that a new research area is copied from (packs.create_pack). Keys starting with '_about' explain the key after them and are ignored by the app -- keep or delete them. See README.md for the whole guide.
_about_id: The pack's id: lower-case letters, digits and '_', starting with a letter. Set when the pack is created; don't change it later (remembered variables and categories are stored under it).
_about_label: The name shown in the app ('Research area').
label: Template (new research area)
_about_description: One or two sentences: what kind of papers and what one row of the dataset is.
description: The starting point of a new research area: example columns, one example extraction stage and example rules, each explained. Replace them with your own.
_about_is_template: true only for this template: it hides the pack from every list in the app. A pack created from it gets false.
_about_template: The file listing the dataset's columns in order (and a vocabulary of compound names, if any). See columns.json.
_about_standard_columns: Optional: more columns with a description each (standard_columns.json). Columns of the extraction stages (stages/*.json) are added automatically, so most packs leave this empty.
_about_species_cids: Optional: PubChem identities of the vocabulary's compounds (a file like the prebiotic pack's species_cids.json). '' = none.
_about_builtin_stages: Extraction steps written in code that this pack uses. Available: 'chemistry' (dissolved species and their concentrations / yields -- built for solution chemistry), 'fit_models' (how astronomical fits were made). Most new packs use none: their extraction is the stages in stages/*.json.
_about_postprocess: Calculations run on the extracted rows, in order. Each is code in the app; the ones that exist are listed in README.md. A new pack usually starts with none.
_about_formulas: Calculations without code: each fills its column on every row where its inputs have values, after the review, in this order. 'expression' uses column names (in backticks when they contain - % ( )), numbers, + - * / **, and functions like first(), ifelse(), sum_of("pattern") -- the full list is in README.md and in the editor's Formulas tab. 'if_present': check (keep the paper's value, flag a difference), keep, or replace. This EXAMPLE adds temperature_K: replace or remove it.
_about_units: What the pack calls a group of rows ('set') and one row ('sample'), used in the prompts and messages. Optionally 'row' for messages ('object model instance').
_about_compact_text: true collapses long runs of spaces in the paper text sent to the model (saves ~20% on table-heavy papers).
_about_focused_row_plan: true: a focused search plans each paper's rows like a full extraction (more accurate rows, a little more cost).
_about_shared_columns: Columns the paper's experiments normally share (methods, instruments): when every row with measured results that states one has the same value, the rows that don't state it get it too -- assumed and flagged, one entry per column (calculators/shared_values.py). By variable category ids, column names, regex 'patterns'; 'exclude' keeps a column out. {} = off.
_about_group_columns: The same within a group of related rows (an experiment set, then a figure or table): when the group's rows that state a column agree, its other rows get the value -- assumed and flagged. Same selector format as shared_columns.
_about_column_pairs: Related columns: when at least two rows give both and they are equal in every one, a row giving one gets the other (e.g. a sampled temperature equal to the initial one) -- assumed and flagged.
_about_label_columns: The column a quantity in a row's own label (in the row plan, e.g. '150 C, 20 min') fills when the row has no column of that kind -- by unit kind: temperature, time, pressure, concentration (only the named compound's column), pH, ... Values contradicting their row's label are flagged either way.
_about_variable_categories: Categories for variables the model suggests beyond the columns (shown in the review and used to place columns). Shared ones -- Metadata, Experimental Methodology, Other -- exist already. Fields: id, label, description (the model reads it), value_type (number / text / any), max_words, table_order (lower = further left), model_assigns (the model may put suggestions in it), patterns (regexes of column names placed in it). Can also be edited in the app (Variables > Variable categories).

variable_categories.label: Conditions
variable_categories.description: a quantity the experiment ran under that has no column (one number with its unit)

variable_categories.label: Results
variable_categories.description: a measured result that has no column (one number with its unit)

_about_category_columns: Which columns sit in which category (the order of the CSV and the Rows tab): {category id: {columns: [...], patterns: [regex, ...]}}. Columns in no category go under Other.
